messages:
Maya R: Heads-up — AcmeProd just flagged a major latency regression after we rolled the new quantization profile to their dedicated pool. p50 is fine but p95/p99 spiked. Customer reports interactive chat latency hitting 2s+ at p99. Included their trace IDs and sample request IDs.

Alex W: thanks — do we have the deployment id / model variant?

Maya R: deployment_id=dep-0a1b2c3, model=rw-gpt-3b-quant-int8-v2, quant_profile: int8-calibrated-2026-03. They flipped the quant profile yesterday 03:10 UTC. Attached from customer:
- repro command they run: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H \"Authorization: Bearer <key>\" -d '{"model":"dep-0a1b2c3","input":"summarize: ..."}'`
- trace ids: t-9f2e3 / t-9f2e4 / t-9f2e5 (multiple slow ones)
- before/after latencies: p95 from ~220ms -> ~460ms, p99 from ~750ms -> ~2350ms during peak. p50 steady ~120ms.

Danielle (oncall): sre-bot, can we pull recent tail latencies for dep-0a1b2c3 and show kernel / device metrics?

sre-bot: alert: deployment dep-0a1b2c3 exceeded p99 latency threshold (1.5s) at 2026-03-15T03:12:xxZ. Samples captured: 42.
Attached logs: `gpu_util: 69% | kernel: attention_opt_v3 | batch_size: 1 | kv_cache_hits: 9%`

Alex W: interesting the kernel shows attention_opt_v3 — that kernel path is selected for int8 variants and sometimes has higher per-token overhead for short sequences vs fp16 (due to extra dequant/quant ops). Does the customer use short-turn-by-turn prompts?

Maya R: yes they said interactive chat, mostly short messages (~30 tokens). Also said they saw it immediately after the profile flip.

Jordi (eng-ml): this matches a known calibration artifact: int8 calibration can increase branching or force slower kernels for short sequences if the per-token quantization path adds extra memcpy or extra kernel launches. We recently changed the lookup table alignment in int8-2026-03 which helps throughput for long sequences but regresses short-seq latency.

Alex W: immediate mitigations: 1) rollback quant_profile for that deployment to fp16-compatible profile, 2) temporarily enable fallback policy to use fp16 variant for <64-token requests, 3) adjust batching to favor 1-request batching with lower wait threshold.

Maya R: customer asked for steps we can do now — can we toggle fallback without a full rollback?

Alex W: yes — you can patch the route config without redeploy:

```yaml
# patch snippet (can apply via console or api)
route_overrides:
  - match: { max_input_tokens: 64 }
    model_variant: rw-gpt-3b-fp16-compat
    policy: immediate-fallback
```
Or via CLI: `redwood routes patch dep-0a1b2c3 --set 'route_overrides[0].model_variant=rw-gpt-3b-fp16-compat'`

Maya R: on it — applying fallback now and will ask customer to repro.

Support Bot: action_log: route override applied by Maya R at 2026-03-15T03:22:18Z (change id: ch-7782bf).

sre-bot: deploy tracer updated: now routing ~34% of short requests to fp16 variant, 66% still to int8 while canary runs.

Maya R: customer tried a few requests — their p99 dropped from ~2.3s to ~240ms for the short-message test. They say interactive feel is back.

Alex W: great — follow-up items:
- eng-ml to re-evaluate int8-2026-03 calibration for short-seq behavior (Jordi)
- eng-runtime to add an automatic short-seq kernel check and prefer fp16 kernels for <64 tokens when int8 path increases tail latency (Alex)
- Support to keep customer on fallback for 24–48h while we validate (Maya)

Jordi (eng-ml): I'll run a targeted micro-benchmark: varying sequence lengths 8..256 with int8-2026-03 vs fp16; collect kernel launch counts and memcpy timings. Probable fix: change quant_scale align or add a small fused dequant kernel for short sequences.

Danielle (oncall): keeping alert open until p99 stable under threshold for 6h. I'll annotate incident channel and tag engineering owners.

Maya R: created ticket RED-8451 (customer-impact, priority: high) capturing repro steps, logs, rollout id, and mitigation applied. I'll also add the sample curl and the route patch snippet.

Alex W: for longer-term we should expose a developer knob: `prefer_low_latency_small_sequences: true/false` in quant profiles so customers can opt in. Also document tradeoffs in the console UI.

Maya R: customer accepted the mitigation and wants a postmortem once we have root cause. They asked if we can proactively scan dedicated pools that got int8-2026-03 and surface any with a p95 jump for short sequences.

Jordi (eng-ml): will add a calibration verification job: after profile release we run a quick seq-length sensitivity check and raise flag if p95>1.5x baseline for any bucket.

Alex W: closing loop — MX notes: rollback not needed thanks to route override. Add to release notes: int8-2026-03 known short-sequence regression.

Maya R: thanks everyone. I'll keep channel updated if customer sees anything else. :thumbsup:

Danielle (oncall): closing alert in 6h if stable.

sre-bot: alert annotated (owner: Danielle).

Jordi (eng-ml): quick action item list saved in RED-8451: [microbench, calibration tweak, expose knob, add verification job].

Maya R: marking thread resolved for support; will update customer when eng team has RCA.

Alex W: thanks — nice fast mitigation.
